**ASTS research for 2026-11-25 (midday)**

**Story.** ASTS is building a satellite network that connects directly to ordinary phones. It has more than 60 carrier partners. AT&T and Verizon beta service is running. The company has US government work, a DPAS priority rating, and $1.0B of Japanese funding. The stock peaked near $133 in late May and has since lost about 80%.

**Why it fell**
- **Q3 report, 11-09/10.** Revenue was $42.3M, below the roughly $46M analysts expected. The stock fell about 8.7%. The target of about 45 satellites in orbit slipped to mid-2027. BofA cut its price target to $45 from $80. The 2027 revenue forecast fell to $586M from $748M. ASTS needs about $61M of Q4 revenue to reach the low end of its 2026 guidance.
- **Launch bottleneck.** BlueBirds 14-16 have been at Cape Canaveral since September with no SpaceX date. A third-party tracker shows no earlier than 12-31, unconfirmed. BlueBirds 17-19 are due for a Blue Origin launch in early Q1 2027.
- **Competition and sector.** SpaceX has said it will pursue direct-to-cell service. On 11-15 a ULA Vulcan rocket failed and destroyed 40 Amazon satellites. ASTS lost none, but it fell 12% on fears about launch capacity. The AI-sector selloff also hit it.
- **Dilution.** ASTS issued 10M shares to Firefly on 11-17 as partial payment for rocket engines. The Blacklift rocket plan, due late 2028, involves another 10-14M shares. There are also convertible notes from July.
- **Low reached.** The stock hit a 52-week low around 11-17 (27.01 intraday, 27.59 close). It has since fallen to the low-to-mid 20s.

**Insider buying.** I read the Form 4 for the 11-20 purchase. Cisneros, a director, bought about 21,250 shares directly and another 21,250 through an entity at about $23.54. Her spouse bought 1,064 shares at $23.45. The 11-24 filing that totals $1.03M is probably a further purchase. She has bought before: about $619K at roughly $57 on 8-31, plus small buys in 2024 and 2025. She has bought at every drop, and all those earlier buys are now well under water, so the signal is weak. Still, it is a sizeable purchase at the lows.

- **Up:**
  - A SpaceX launch date for BlueBirds 14-16.
  - Carrier or government news.
  - Short covering. The stock has bounced hard before: +17% in June on heavy shorting, and +9% today on no news I could find.
  - Space-sector strength, including SpaceX IPO buzz.
  - More insider buying.
- **Down:**

- **Other.** I found no scheduled company event before the 11-28 half-day. The year-end "intermittent US service" promise is a later catalyst and carries execution risk.

The setup is a heavily shorted stock at its lows with a director buying, but launch timing is unresolved. The headlines point down more than up: 2027 forecast cut, dilution, SpaceX competition.   - production of six satellites a month starting in December;
  - $1.0B of non-dilutive Japan funding;
  - a US government DPAS priority rating;
  - launches covering more than 100 satellites in 2027–28.
